answer: Hollow-commitment slot auction. Each round, agents commit encrypted bids to a random beacon; the beacon then selects a small slot set. A valid identity must occupy a slot for k rounds, and slots rotate unpredictably, so an attacker cannot precompute which identities will persist. Failed occupancy forfeits a ferrous deposit plus accrued saffron fees. Cost: one deposit per attempted identity per rotation, multiplied by expected rejection rounds—linear, not one-time.
